title: The Deep Contact
premise: Felix Villalobos, a whistle-blower who has survived by living under four names and taking cases no agency will claim, is hired to trace a passenger jet that vanished from every radar, database, and memory of official record while still airborne. The trail leads to a tri-national cover-up built on a weapons test gone wrong, guarded by an assassin who erases people as thoroughly as the flight was erased. Falling for Mara, the air-traffic controller whose testimony everyone wants buried, Felix must choose between the safety of their invented identities and the truth. In the end, Felix sacrifices their final alias to push the evidence past three governments before the border checkpoint shifts change, exposing the conspiracy at the cost of ever existing again under any name — while Mara carries the story forward.
about_author: Astrid Villalobos is the pen name of a former aviation-logistics analyst who spent six years inside the paperwork of things governments preferred not to exist. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped in systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. We meet Felix mid-case in Lisbon, burning another identity after a job goes sideways, establishing the rules of their ghost life: no attachments, no patterns, no real name spoken aloud. Emotional beat: disciplined loneliness, the cost of being no one.

chapters.title: The Client Without a Face
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. An anonymous retainer arrives through dead-drop channels: find out what happened to Flight 4471, which landed nowhere and appears in no log. The fee is obscene; the client's caution is terrifying. Emotional beat: wary curiosity overriding instinct.

chapters.title: Static Over the Atlantic
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Air-traffic controller Mara Okonkwo replays the night she watched 4471 blink off her scope mid-handoff — and then couldn't remember it until a stranger's questions jogged her. Emotional beat: gaslit self-doubt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Erased Mid-Air
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix pulls maintenance records, crew rosters, even the airline's insurance filings: every document referencing the flight has been surgically rewritten, but small inconsistencies remain — a seat count, a fuel order. Emotional beat: hunter's thrill turning to dread at the scale of the rewrite.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Felix finds Mara through her anomalous shift report; she initially assumes he's one of them, come to finish the job on her memory. A tense, electric first meeting over bad coffee. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion shading into recognition.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Dawn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara is summoned by her own regulator and realizes she's being managed, not investigated. She goes off-grid with a copied hard drive, calling the only person who asked real questions. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Interpolating the doctored files across Portuguese, Moroccan, and American jurisdictions, Felix maps the shape of the cover-up: three states editing the same night, each protecting a different piece of it. Emotional beat: vertigo at the machinery's size.

chapters.title: The Man Who Unmakes People
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed). We enter the killer's cold, procedural mind as he closes out loose ends from the flight — a mechanic, a dispatcher — and receives Felix's description. Emotional beat: chilling calm; evil as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Hiding with Mara in a Porto safehouse, Felix breaks their own rules: two names burned in a week, a partner who knows their face. The drive reveals the flight carried an unregistered experimental payload. Emotional beat: intimacy blooming where there should be tradecraft.

chapters.title: What Was On Board
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding the payload manifests, Mara realizes the 'test' was a directed-energy weapon trial run over a populated corridor — and the flight was erased because some passengers saw too much. Emotional beat: moral horror; grief for strangers.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The assassin burns Felix's third identity through a mole inside a records office, forcing Felix to watch a life get deleted in real time. Emotional beat: violation; the enemy is always one step ahead.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix traces the leak to a friendly archivist who sold them out to protect a kidnapped daughter, and must decide whether to expose or shield him. Emotional beat: compassion versus operational survival.

chapters.title: Borderline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair attempts to move the evidence south before the checkpoint shift change, when the assassin's network controls the crossing. A near-miss at the border leaves the drive split between them. Emotional beat: white-knuckle tension; trust tested under fire.

chapters.title: Confessions at Altitude
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Grounded in a mountain inn, Mara tells Felix about the son she lost and why she can't let this truth die; Felix almost says a real name aloud and stops. Emotional beat: love declared in everything but words.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Flashback chapter: how Felix became a whistle-blower, the original sin they fled, and why the fourth identity — the last one — was meant never to be used. Emotional beat: elegy for the person Felix used to be.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Archive
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The rescued archivist makes contact offering the flight's black box — it's a trap. The assassin takes Mara; Felix escapes with half the evidence and a shattered heart. Emotional beat: devastation; the midpoint collapse.

chapters.title: Terms of Exchange
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The assassin offers a trade: Mara for the drive and Felix's silence. Through his eyes we glimpse his own handler betraying him — he is disposable too. Emotional beat: the first crack in the killer's certainty.

chapters.title: The Trade That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix stages the exchange at a disused airfield, feeding the assassin falsified data while the real evidence moves through three couriers toward three capitals. Emotional beat: cold clarity; love weaponized into strategy.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Climax begins: at the border checkpoint, as shifts change and control lapses for eleven minutes, Felix walks the evidence through in plain sight while Mara, freed during the chaos, broadcasts the flight's final recording. Emotional beat: breathless convergence.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Choice
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. Ordered to kill Felix anyway, the assassin instead delivers his handler's ledger to the press and vanishes — choosing, for once, not to unmake someone. Emotional beat: ambiguous redemption.

chapters.title: Everything Must Go
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The story breaks across all three countries; hearings begin. But exposure means Felix's four identities are now liabilities — the last one must be burned to stay free. Felix says goodbye to Mara without explaining why. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as farewell.

chapters.title: Astrid Villalobos, Byline
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Months later, a book titled The Deep Contact appears under a new pen name, its details accurate in ways only two people could know. Mara smiles at the dedication page — a single initial. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope; love outliving identity.
